messages:
Jess: Heads up — after the runtime merge that landed this morning (abc123) our canary shows a clear decode-path p95 regression (~30%). CI perf test `decode_p95_shortseq` failed in the canary run. Flamegraph + perf log in the thread below.

Arun: :eyes: saw that alert. Any quick repro steps?

Jess: Repro locally with the canary docker image. Steps: `./run_canary.sh --model redwood-small --seq 32 --threads 8 --requests 2000`. Repro script attached.

Liam: I pulled the flamegraph — looks like the attention kernel chooser spends more time in the fallback path, plus a larger proportion of time in fused-op scheduler. Not a pure memory pressure thing.

Sasha: Can you paste the short profiler snippet?

Jess: Paste:```
CPU: decode_task_loop 40%
GPU: attn_kernel_selector 28% -> fallback_kernel 18%
GPU: fused_op_scheduler 22% (queue stall)
KV cache ops small but frequent thrash on small batches
```

Arun: Interesting. The selector change in abc123 altered the threshold that picks the tiled attention kernel vs the fallback. On short sequences that can push us into a path with higher kernel launch overhead.

Liam: Also seeing more small batches due to the batching heuristic change in that PR. Batcher now aggressively flushes after 8ms; for shortseq workload that increases kernel-invocation count.

Jess: CI logs show `decode_p95_shortseq` increased from 38ms -> 50ms. Canary traces show many 2–6ms kernel launches instead of fewer ~10–20ms launches.

Sasha: Is this reproducible on A100 and T4?

Liam: I ran both. A100 shows the same relative regression; T4 has larger absolute impact. So kernel-launch overhead matters across HW.

ci-bot: CI perf test `decode_p95_shortseq` FAILED in canary (job/5678). Full log: https://ci.internal/jobs/5678

Arun: Let's bisect quickly between abc122 (pre) and abc123 (post). If the selector threshold change is the culprit we can revert that small block.

Jess: I started a local git bisect and found the change narrows to commit abc123: the selector now uses `seq_len / tile_size` heuristic instead of latency-model estimate.

Liam: Workaround idea: temporarily increase batcher flush threshold to coalesce short requests and prefer the tiled kernel. Can we push a canary config change (no code) to test?

Sasha: We can try config change first — lower `batch_max_flush_ms` from 8 -> 20 in canary config. That should reduce small-batch churn.

Jess: Deployed canary-config change. Monitoring metrics...

devops-bot: Canary config update applied to pool/rw-canary at 2024-09-12T14:12:03Z

Jess: Early numbers: p95 dropped from 50ms -> 41ms after config tweak. Still above baseline but much closer.

Arun: Good. That suggests batching heuristic + selector interplay. Still want to revert selector change that favors tile_count rule. If we revert selector and keep batching tweak, we might be at baseline.

Liam: Agreed. I'll open a revert PR for the selector diff and add a test to cover shortseq kernel choice.

Sasha: Also add a perf unit test that simulates high small-batch rate so future merges exercise this path in CI.

Jess: For transparency — canary hold recommended until revert lands. This is a rollout blocker for larger regions.

Arun: Can we add an automatic fallback to prefer the lower-latency kernel if launch_count > X within sliding window? That would be defensive.

Liam: That's a decent medium-term fix. Short term revert + config roll should buy us time. I'll draft the revert PR now: PR #4399.

ci-bot: PR #4399 opened by Liam — "revert: selector heuristic -> latency-model". CI: running perf checks.

Sasha: Once the revert merges, we should roll canary forward and run the `decode_p95_shortseq` perf job; if green, promote.

Jess: Also documenting the incident: add a quick note to the perf-regressions board and tag the model infra owners.

Arun: Thanks all. Next actions: (1) Liam lands revert PR, (2) Sasha adds perf unit test + CI perf check, (3) Keep canary flush config until we validate.

Liam: On it. Will update thread with PR link + perf run results.

Jess: :thumbsup:
